analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing
key_insights: JPM Market Intelligence stays Tactically Bullish and expects a Tech rebound. When the NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it has tended to rebound about 3% the following week, and the effect is stronger when the decline lands on a Friday.
Last week the SPX fell 56bp, NDX fell 2%, and RTY rose 1.3%. AI fears pushed NDX down 4.8% over the last two trading days. 9 of 11 SPX sectors rose and all outperformed the index.

JPM's preferred Monetization Menu (Nov 2) is a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals. Consumers and Financials can keep working if the yield curve steepens. Europe could catch a bid if a US/Iran deal progresses. In Jan-Feb, US Value was +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.

Midterm scenario odds from BBG prediction markets as of Nov 1: Blue Wave 66% (SPX -25bp to +50bp), Split Congress Dem House/GOP Senate 26% (SPX +0.5% to +1%), Red Wave 7% (SPX +1% to +1.25%), GOP House/Dem Senate 1% (SPX +25bp to +75bp).

In a Blue Wave, JPM sees AI regulation as hard to pass because Trump has said he will not sign bills that limit AI expansion and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority. The risk is that the market uses the added liquidity to de-gross within the AI theme. Lower deficit spending may slightly reduce longer-dated yields.

SPX has been up a year after every midterm election since 1950, with an average gain of around 15%. On a 3-month basis the SPX has averaged +5.4%, on 6-month +11.4%, 9-month +12.5% and 12-month +14.7%. The 6, 9 and 12-month returns have a 100% hit rate dating to 1990.

JPM argues that this week's data can ease stagflation and recession fears. It cites record household net worth and strong cash balances, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant driver of hiring. It expects an AI capex decline to hit GDP metrics more than labor markets or spending.

JPM's biggest non-AI risk is a Middle East re-escalation. It cites a WSJ report of Iranian damage to US regional bases and depleted munitions, which suggests another wave of attacks could be limited in scope and duration. It sees oil as already pricing the outcome, so there is limited upside for energy prices and limited room for yields to move and equities to fall.

The BBG 2027 Fair Value WTI swap trades at about $88 against $65-$70 normal prices, and Brent trades about $20/bbl above what fundamentals imply. JPM says this leaves fewer oil or Energy equity long hedges to offset equity losses, and that adding downside protection may be prudent.

AAPL preview from Samik Chatterjee: 26Q4 revenue of $112.9bn (+10% YoY), modestly above the guidance midpoint. He forecasts 27Q1 revenue of $147.9bn (+3% YoY) with iPhone revenue of $84.0bn (-2% YoY) on units of 69mm (-18% YoY). His FY27 revenue forecast is $518.3bn (+9% YoY), just below consensus.

FactSet earnings update with 60% of the SPX reported: blended revenue growth is 13.4%, EPS growth 30.2%, and margins 14.9%. Mag7 blended EPS growth is 22.6% against 32.6% for the SPX493, which would be the first time Mag7 growth has been lower since 22Q4.

Macro: initial 26Q3 real GDP growth was 3.4%, with headline PCE at 3.6% YoY and core PCE at 3.1%, both higher than the prior month. Feroli expects ISM-Mfg of 54.5, ISM-Services of 55.5 and NFP of +75k, with the unemployment rate falling to 4.1%.

Technicals (Jason Hunter): the S&P 500 is in a choppy range above key support at 7616-7643, with other short-term levels near 7500. A break below could take the index to the 7200s and then to 7000 as trend-following selling builds. He is also watching the SOX Index range support at about 10400-11000 and KOSPI at about 5000.

Vol (Jade Bassil): the spot/vol correlation in NDX is the least negative it has ever been. Drivers include low positioning, market makers holding a lot of vega, levered ETF AUM up 40% YTD, auto-call and exotic issuance, and spot at all-time highs.

Positioning Intelligence: global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis. The October MTD estimate is -2.6% through Oct 29, likely near -3.5% after Friday. The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile, and retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile.
Pre-market Nov 2: SPX +0.5%, NDX +0.8%, RTY +0.8%. WTI fell 4.2% to $99.84 on Middle East diplomatic optimism. The 10Y yield is 4.917% and VIX is 18.90.

market_movers.rationale: Samik Chatterjee forecasts 26Q4 revenue of $112.9bn (+10% YoY), modestly above the guidance midpoint. He raises FY27 estimates to reflect durable growth, with revenue of $518.3bn just below consensus.

sector_views.rationale: Broadening is expected to continue, with Consumers and Financials working if the curve steepens. JPM weights the Tech and Cyclicals barbell toward Cyclicals.
JPM expects a tactical rebound but a more selective market between AI winners and losers.
US Banks have a strong November seasonal record, Financials ETFs saw the strongest inflows last week, and HFs remain net long Banks.
Oil appears to have priced a resumption of hostilities, so JPM sees limited upside for energy prices and fewer long hedges against equity losses.

earnings_insights: AAPL 26Q4 (reports Nov 2 AMC): JPM estimate of revenue $112.9bn, +10% YoY, modestly above the guidance midpoint. This is a forecast, not a reported figure.
AAPL 27Q1 (estimate): revenue $147.9bn, +3% YoY, iPhone revenue $84.0bn, -2% YoY, on 69mm units, -18% YoY. Samik Chatterjee's forecast, not a reported figure.
AAPL FY27 (estimate): revenue $518.3bn, +9% YoY, with iPhone revenue $273.2bn, +8% YoY, on about 247mm units, +3% YoY. This is just below consensus.
FactSet blended (actual plus forecast) with 60% of the SPX reported: revenue growth 13.4%, EPS growth 30.2%, profit margins 14.9%.
Mag7 blended EPS growth is 22.6% against 32.6% for the SPX493, and consensus for 26Q4 is 22.6% for Mag7 against 30.8% for SPX493.
7 of 11 sectors are seeing margin improvement, led by Energy and Tech. Margins are compressing in Financials (-30bp QoQ), Discretionary (-30bp) and Staples (-10bp).
GOOG's post-earnings move of -12.5% was its worst one-day performance ever, per Craig Cohen.
Earnings Nov 2 AMC include AAPL, PLTR, ON, VRTX, ROKU, WMB and FANG. Nov 3 AMC include AMD, AMGN, ANET, BKNG and SMCI. Nov 4 AMC include QCOM, APP, SNAP and HUBS.

risk_factors: Re-escalation in the Middle East after the US midterms.
An AI trade sell-off, including capital raise, circular financing and legal concerns, and AI hardware groups breaking multi-month range support.
A Blue Wave in which the market uses added liquidity to de-gross within the AI theme.
A break of S&P 500 support at 7616-7643, with potential selling toward the 7200s and then 7000 as trend-following selling builds.
Quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
Persistent elevated inflation, with headline PCE at 3.6% and core PCE at 3.1%.
Bearish pressure spilling from Tech into cyclically sensitive groups.
charts_described: SPX returns Jan-Feb 2026 chart, per the text, shows US Value +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.
The text describes a chart of S&P 500 key support at 7616-7643 and CTA trigger levels (50-day, 100-day, 1-month momentum) clustered in that area.
vol_and_positioning: NDX spot/vol correlation is the least negative it has ever been, with more spot up/vol up and spot down/vol down behavior.
Skew has not realized because the market has seen more rotations than large correlated sell-offs. Market makers are still holding a lot of vega.
Levered ETF AUM is up 40% YTD, and auto-call and exotic issuance is growing on NDX and single names.
Global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis, and the global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD.
Prior -3z events in the 20-day L-S performance spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases, averaging +1%.
Momentum exposure is at 12-month-plus lows. Risks include potential Quant de-grossing and still-elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows are +1z, and CTA positioning is at the 44th percentile in US equities.
The Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) has rallied to 2-year highs.
Social media sentiment and the TMT-Defensives spread are both at the 6th percentile, similar to prior episodes that were followed by Tech-led rebounds.
EU positioning bounced from the 5th to the 14th percentile. China/HK positioning is at the 5th percentile, the most bearish of any major region.
JPM suggests adding some downside protection for equity investors.
geopolitical: US/Iran conflict: US troops have been engaged beyond 90 days without Congressional approval. Democrats could pull funding or force a troop removal, but only after the new Congress is seated in January.
WSJ and AP report that Iran damaged 119 buildings across 13 US installations in the first two weeks of the war, which challenges earlier Pentagon statements.
Reports of depleted US weapons inventories call into question the intensity and duration of another wave of attacks.
The US approved a possible $2.1bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine, a few hours after Ukraine hit its first refinery in 2 weeks.
The US and China have agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
The US midterm elections are on Nov 3. The government funding deadline is Dec 11 and the G20 summit is Dec 15-16.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM expects a tactical Tech rebound. After a 3.5%+ NDX decline near ATH, it has tended to rebound about 3% the next week, and HF de-risking and a 6th percentile TMT sentiment gap echo prior lows that preceded Tech-led rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: AI fears around capital raises, circular financing and legal issues, plus lack of capitulation and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning, could keep pressure on. Hunter is watching AI hardware range supports (SOX ~10400-11000, KOSPI ~5000).
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below S&P 500 support at 7616-7643 could take the index to the 7200s and then to 7000.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump has said he will not sign bills that limit AI expansion and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority, so AI regulation is hard to pass. A dip would be a buying opportunity.
tension_points.bear_case: A Blue Wave could prompt de-grossing within the AI theme on higher assumed regulation and liquidity, and 'investigation risk' for MegaCap Tech leaders tied to Trump donations.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil already prices the outcome, so there is limited upside for energy prices, bond yields and equity downside. Depleted munitions and base damage may point to heightened diplomatic efforts.
tension_points.bear_case: Another wave of attacks would hit equities with fewer oil or Energy equity long hedges available, and the Brent premium of about $20/bbl shows geopolitical risk is large.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US/Iran deal would support Europe and Value and reduce the geopolitical premium.
